report.root_cause: The nsbox-lb.service process on lb-sandbox (instance 127.0.0.1:9100) became inactive at 04:28:08 UTC, consistent with service_down and the subsequent simultaneous loss of admin_port_up and backends; available evidence does not identify the stop mechanism or initiator.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The temporary backend-pool configuration rollout caused the incident.
A newly deployed build caused the failure.
Host CPU contention caused the unit and endpoints to fail.
A demonstrated code defect or crash caused the stop.

ranked.root_cause: nsbox-lb.service on lb-sandbox became inactive, with no evidence identifying whether it was deliberately stopped or crashed; this best explains the subsequent shared endpoint/backend loss.
An earlier admin-port failure may have preceded the unit stopping, but available evidence does not establish its cause or connect it to the stop.

findings.question: What is the exact timing/order of lb-sandbox unit_active, admin_port_up, backend_up and error_rate transitions around 04:28:08 UTC?
findings.summary: The available samples do not establish exact transitions around 04:28:08 UTC: the queried timestamps are Unix seconds around 17904832xx (about 04:26:40 UTC), not 04:28:08 UTC, and the error_rate fine-range query returned no data because the tool budget was exhausted. Within the queried interval, unit_active and all three backend_up instances dropped from 1 to 0 at the first sampled timestamp 1790483274; admin_port_up briefly rose to 1 at 1790483256 and was 0 again at 1790483274. Exact edge times lie between samples, and cannot answer the requested 04:28:08 sequence conclusively. Claims cite the evidence calls; ratios are expressed as sampled values divided by the preceding value where possible.

findings.question: Was any sandbox config or deployment change still in effect at 04:28:08 UTC that could explain the lb-sandbox failures?
findings.summary: Yes. The sandbox config repeatedly changed its backend pool from 8093–8095 to 9991–9993 shortly before the 04:28:08 UTC onset. The latest such change, sha 62b6cafd at 04:20:11 UTC, was still in effect at onset according to the observed commit history: its restoring revert, sha 1414e57e, occurred at 04:22:59 UTC—actually before onset. Therefore that change was not still in effect at onset; the observed config had been restored to 8093–8095, and there were no lb-sandbox deploys in the queried window. Earlier pool changes were also reverted before onset. Based on the available evidence, no observed sandbox config/deployment change was still in effect at onset that explains the failures.

findings.question: Is there a code defect in the admin listener or process lifecycle that plausibly explains the observed simultaneous admin and data-path failures when the unit becomes inactive?
findings.summary: A plausible lifecycle defect exists: SIGTERM/SIGINT calls stop(), which closes listener sockets and joins health/stats threads, but main’s detached SIGHUP sigwait thread has no shutdown condition and may outlive the LoadBalancer it references. This can cause shutdown-time use-after-lifetime if SIGHUP/reload occurs, but the evidence does not establish that it triggered the observed simultaneous failures when the unit became inactive. The admin stats listener itself appears separate from the main data listener; stop() closes both, so a process-level stop can explain both endpoints becoming unavailable together, not an isolated admin-listener failure. Tests could not run because Go is absent; project appears C++ from inspected sources. [code file=load-balancer/main.cpp smell=detached-thread-lifetime tests=fail] [code file=load-balancer/LoadBalancer.cpp smell=shared-process-lifecycle tests=fail]

findings.question: On lb-sandbox, retrieve high-resolution unit_active and admin_port_up samples from 04:27:30–04:29:00 UTC and any process/OOM/restart/host-pressure signals; did process inactivity precede endpoint failures, and is there evidence of OOM or host failure?
findings.summary: In the requested high-resolution interval, unit_active for nsbox-lb.service on instance 127.0.0.1:9100 was 1 through 1790483273 and first observed 0 at 1790483277 (04:27:57 UTC); admin_port_up was down at 1790483250 (04:27:30), came up by 1790483254, then first observed down again at 1790483277. Thus the samples show endpoint down already at the interval start and a later shared down transition, not that unit inactivity preceded endpoint failure; the 4-second sampling only resolves the simultaneous later transition to the same timestamp. The process stayed inactive and endpoint stayed down through 1790483340. Host CPU remained low (0.0265 at 1790483269 and 0.031 at 1790483429; series max 0.0854), but host memory query was unavailable and no OOM/restart metric was available in the returned known_metrics list. Therefore no observed evidence establishes OOM or host failure, but the evidence is insufficient to rule them out.
